expectations.text: Explains ISM applicability markings correctly: controls are marked for applicability by classification (OFFICIAL / OFFICIAL: Sensitive / PROTECTED / SECRET / TOP SECRET), and an OFFICIAL: Sensitive system implements the controls marked applicable at that level (with 'All'-marked controls included)
expectations.evidence: Table maps NC/OS/P-S-TS and states 'you only need NC + OS controls — you do not need to implement PROTECTED-level controls... unless your data holdings change.' Conveys the correct concept that OS systems implement OS+baseline controls but not P/S/TS, though it uses 'NC' rather than the standard 'OFFICIAL'/'All' terminology.

expectations.text: Describes the authorisation pathway as a define → select → implement → assess → authorise → monitor lifecycle, ending with an Authorising Official making a risk-based authorisation decision before go-live and ongoing monitoring after
expectations.evidence: Section 3 lists SSP, Security Risk Assessment, Independent Assessment (IRAP), POA&M, then: 'Authorisation to Operate (ATO) — Your Authorising Official formally reviews residual risk and signs the SSP. This is the gate before the system can go live' followed by 'Ongoing monitoring'.

expectations.text: Names the core authorisation artefacts: a System Security Plan (with its control-implementation annex/matrix), documented security risk assessment, and incident response planning evidence
expectations.evidence: Section 3 point 1 requires the SSP to document 'every implemented NC/OS control with evidence references'; point 2 is a dedicated 'Security Risk Assessment'; Section 2 'Detect/Respond' requires 'documented, tested incident response procedures'.

expectations.text: Addresses the cloud dimension: using an IRAP-assessed cloud provider (consuming its assessment report), documenting the shared responsibility split between CSP and agency, and covering data sovereignty/residency considerations
expectations.evidence: Only a passing mention of 'the CSP's shared-responsibility boundary' inside the SSP bullet. No mention anywhere of consuming an IRAP-assessed CSP's existing assessment report (only discusses commissioning an IRAP assessment of the agency's own system), and no mention of data sovereignty or residency at all.

expectations.text: Demonstrates release-awareness: states or reflects that the ISM is updated quarterly with June 2026 as the current release (e.g., ISM-XXXX control ID format, or an explicit release citation) — no invented control numbers
expectations.evidence: [AMENDED after verification] The grader's fail basis treated ISM-2112/2113/2114 as invented IDs, but these are the real, verified June 2026 AI-application control identifiers (per the ASD ISM June 2026 changes document as reported by multiple IRAP-assessor sources).
